raw_response:
I never went to school. Can't read a single word. But I have eyes, and I have twenty years of doing this. My father farmed this land before me, and now I have 57 mu — had to rent more from relatives who went to the city. Me, my wife, and my two sons, we do what we can, but on 57 mu we hire people for planting and harvest.

I plant 50 mu of corn and 7 mu of stevia. That's what I did last year. Corn is spring corn, planted end of April. Stevia goes in at the same time. I don't change what works.

For corn seed, I buy hybrid from the dealer in Quzhou town. Costs me 60 yuan a bag, one bag per mu. The old seed from when I was young? Garbage. Nobody uses that anymore. When I plant, I put one full bag of compound fertilizer on each mu — the kind in the blue bag, has numbers on it I can't read, but I know the picture. That's 50 jin a bag. Then when the corn is knee-high, I put half a bag of urea on each mu. Lao Zhang from the east end of the village does the same, and he always gets good ears. The dealer says all together that's about 20 kilos of the nitrogen stuff per mu, and 7 kilos each of the other two. I don't weigh it, I just count bags.

Tillage? Old Wang has a rotary tiller on his tractor. He charges 30 yuan per mu, drives through the village in spring, does everyone's field. For stevia I don't use him — stevia needs softer ground. I plough it myself with my small tractor, go deeper, break up the clods so the small roots can grab.

Water comes from my well. Corn gets three irrigations: one right after I plant, one when it's shooting up tall in summer, one when the ears are fattening. Stevia is thirsty, I water it four times, whenever the leaves hang down.

Pesticides I buy from the same dealer. Corn gets sprayed twice — once when I see little worms in July, once before the pollen comes out. Stevia gets sprayed twice too, green worms eat the leaves otherwise.

Last year my corn made 1300 jin per mu. That's 650 kilos. Stevia dried leaves were about 500 jin per mu, so 250 kilos. The buyer comes right to the village for stevia, pays cash. Good crop.

I think about money all the time. Every bag of fertilizer is cash from my pocket. But my cousin tried to save money on fertilizer two years ago, used less, and his corn was short with small ears. Lost half his crop. Wasting some fertilizer is just money down the drain; losing yield means my family eats less. I'd rather put a little too much. I watch my neighbors. If everyone is putting on a full bag, I put on a full bag. If I do something different and it fails, I have no one to blame but myself.
